newsitem.title: USA: Court rules non-native Alaskans can own reindeer.
newsitem.headline: Court rules non-native Alaskans can own reindeer.

text.p: A federal appeals court ruled on Wednesday that non-native Alaskans may own and sell reindeer despite a decades-old law that fostered a native monopoly in the reindeer herding industry.

The 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in San Francisco held that the Reindeer Act of 1937, passed by Congress to preserve the "native character" of the reindeer industry, does not prohibit non-natives in Alaska from owning, importing or selling reindeer.

Contrary to popular belief, reindeer are not native to Alaska. They were brought in from Russia in the early 20th Century because white settlers had nearly exhausted the natural food supply of Alaskan natives, who traditionally relied on fishing and hunting, the court said.

When white settlers tried to muscle into the reindeer business, Congress responded by passing the Reindeer Act, which appropriated $2 million to buy all of the reindeer owned by non-natives in Alaska and give them to the natives. The act also strictly limited the sale of reindeer to non-natives.
A legal dispute over the reindeer act erupted in 1986, when Thomas Williams, a non-native, sought permission to import reindeer to Alaska from Canada for commercial use.
Native reindeer herders objected. The Interior Board of Indian Appeals and a federal trial court ruled against Williams, who argued the act violated his rights.
The federal appeals court reversed the rulings Wednesday.

"Although the act erects a number of barriers to non-native participation in the reindeer industry, it does not prohibit non-natives in Alaska from owning, importing, or selling reindeer," the court said.

Walter Featherly, attorney for Williams, welcomed the ruling. "It's been a very long road to establish that he (Williams) should not be discriminated against on the basis of his race," Featherly said.
Attorneys representing native reindeer herders were not available to comment on the decision.
